question: Does a raw Windows Filtering Platform block keyed to a throwaway account SID refuse that account's outbound connect, with and without the loopback permit filter (arm 1), across a 7,200 s hold with Bitdefender running (arm 2), and can a persistent version be added and removed by key (arm 3a)?

hardware.antivirus: Bitdefender running (bdagent, bdntwrk, bdredline, bdservicehost, bduserhost)

software_arm1_only.model: Qwen3.5-4B INT8 on GPU, operator-run server (spike_model.py serve)

method: Throwaway local account; raw WFP provider/sublayer/filters at ALE_AUTH_CONNECT V4/V6 with a per-SID ALE_USER_ID condition; operator baseline, account baseline (filters absent), filters, account probe, removal verified by key, account run after removal; operator watchdog every 2 s.

arm1_permit_off.account_loopback_request: refused 3 of 3 at the socket, error 10013, 36-39 ms

arm2_hold.bitdefender_update_signal: bitdefender_folder_timestamps_changed (weak: five folders had later last-write times at the end than at the start - 14:42 to 16:42 x3, 14:27 to 16:27, 12:42 to 15:42 - start values predate the hold, periodic-looking two-hour spacing, no new process)

not_measured: a restart (arm 3b not run; persistence across a reboot NOT ESTABLISHED)
a hold across sleep or a Bitdefender engine update
speed of anything under the block
replication_note: Arm 1: six runs within about seven minutes after one restart are a repeat, not independent replications. Arm 2 is one hold; its 120 samples are inside one observation. Arm 3a is one run. No variation across holds, boots or days was measured.
